title: News – Allotrope Foundation
content: Shimadzu LabSolutions Accommodates Output in Internationally Standardized Data Formats August 2026 Shimadzu LabSolutions supports output using data formats specified by the Allotrope Foundation, including the Allotrope Simple Model (ASM) and the Allotrope Data Format (ADF). This capability enables the automated conversion of analytical data into multiple formats, supporting interoperability across different manufacturers and software systems, thus accelerating and streamlining research and development. Read more about the LabSolutions features at Shimadzu . Semantic Modeling in Materials Science and Engineering With Platform MaterialDigital Core Ontology 3.0 July 28, 2026 The Platform MaterialDigital (PMD) project develops a semantic framework for representing and integrating materials-science data, centered on the PMD Core Ontology (PMDco). Its latest research describes PMDco 3.0 and its role in enabling interoperable, knowledge-based materials data; the work also references the Allotrope Foundation Ontology (AFO) as an example of an established domain ontology for scientific data. Read the full research article in Advanced Engineering Materials . Building the foundation for AI-ready next-generation labs: The lab of the future is here. 2026 Life science organizations seeking to accelerate the discovery of new therapies and diagnostics need AI-ready data foundations, particularly for laboratory data. Deloitte’s Lab of the Future solution, developed in collaboration with AWS, helps transform siloed instrument data into reusable data products through intelligent data pipelines. By automatically parsing and standardizing laboratory data into models such as the Allotrope Simple Model (ASM), the solution enables faster insights, improved compliance, and better data accessibility. Read the article at Deloitte . From Data Silos to Data Intelligence: How Open Standards Like Allotrope Are Transforming Scientific Innovation May 25, 2026 In modern life sciences, innovation is often limited not by experimentation but by data fragmentation. Laboratories generate massive volumes of analytical data, yet much of it remains isolated, inconsistent, and underutilized, making it difficult to derive insights and scale AI-driven research. This is where open data standards like the Allotrope Foundation come into play—helping reshape how scientific data is structured, shared, and activated. Read the article at texium solutions . Highlights from the 2026 AWS Life Sciences Symposium: Research and Drug Discovery May 20, 2026 At the 2026 AWS Life Sciences Symposium, AWS highlighted how agentic AI, unified scientific data foundations, and connected laboratory workflows are transforming research and drug discovery. The symposium showcased how organizations are building AI-enabled, lab-in-the-loop environments that connect experimental and computational workflows. AWS also demonstrated AI-assisted development of instrument data converters, achieving a 100% pass rate for Allotrope Simple Model (ASM) format conversion in its evaluation, helping accelerate laboratory data standardization and interoperability. Read the full report on AWS Blogs . Federated Semantic Knowledge Graphs for Laboratory Workflows: A Structured Expert Elicitation Methodology Demonstrated Through Bioanalytical Workflow Twins May 15, 2026 A paper by Biochemical and Cellular Pharmacology Department, Genentech, presents a federated Semantic Knowledge Graph for laboratory workflows that captures tacit expert knowledge, failure modes, and hidden automation risks. Built via structured expert elicitation, it spans ELISA, LC-MS/PRM, and automation systems, aligned through an upper ontology based on the Allotrope Foundation Ontology (AFO) and OBI, extended for epistemic reasoning. A key concept, MASKED_BY, models silent failures where automation reports success while scientific validity is compromised. The framework enables cross-workflow failure and knowledge-gap queries not possible in conventional lab systems. Read the paper at arXiv . ZONTAL Studio - ASM Language Features May 4, 2016 ZONTAL has released ZONTAL Studio – ASM Language Features, a Visual Studio Code extension designed to simplify the creation, editing, and validation of ASM files. The extension provides rich language support for ASM, including syntax highlighting, IntelliSense, schema-driven validation, hover documentation, document formatting, and navigation features. By leveraging ASM manifests, users receive real-time guidance and validation against Allotrope specifications, helping improve data quality and development efficiency. The extension is available free of charge through the Visual Studio Marketplace and can be installed directly from the marketplace listing.
